traps.title: Early defaults are rising in near-prime Flex Plan, while charge-offs still read zero
traps.explanation: Charge-offs cannot appear until about 120 days past due, so a zero charge-off rate 12 weeks after launch says nothing about credit quality. The early-warning signal is the first-payment default rate: for near-prime Flex Plan customers it rose from about 1.8% to over 6% by week 12. Filter to 'Near-prime (below 720)' to see it clearly.

traps.title: Flex Plan growth is partly moved from card balances
traps.explanation: Weekly card interest per Flex Plan customer fell from about $21 to under $10, while Flex Plan interest per customer held near $14. Customers are moving balances from a roughly 24% card APR to a 15.99% Flex Plan. Part of the 'new' volume is existing borrowing at a lower rate, so net value is lower than gross volume suggests.
